page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.large is a general-purpose server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, yielding 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, which translates to 4.0 GB of memory per core. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations.

This instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and it has a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates moderate single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1607.88 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1742.0, both falling in the average range. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core performance score of 1899.38 and the Passmark memory score of 948.41 are categorized as poor, reflecting the constraints of a single physical core.

Due to its hardware profile, the m7i-flex.large is best suited for light general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, and single-threaded applications like text processing or basic compression tasks. It exhibits weak performance in multi-threaded tasks, database operations, and LLM inference, where prompt processing for a 7B model reaches only 13.27 tokens per second. The instance offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads that require modern Intel Xeon features like AMX and DDR5 memory but do not demand high multi-core throughput or local storage.
